# MixOS

> MixOS is an agent-operable computing system: a Linux userland where every app is a service, every service speaks one message bus, and Mix is the shell. It is tried as a small signed systemd-nspawn image that runs on its own virtual terminal beside the user's existing desktop, at native GPU, input and audio speed.

Every page on https://mixos.dev is static HTML at a directory-style URL (`/try/`) and is
also published as Markdown (`/try.md`). The links below point at the Markdown.
`/llms-full.txt` is the whole manual in one file.

## Docs

- [Try it beside your desktop](https://mixos.dev/try.md): How MixOS runs as a small signed systemd-nspawn image on its own virtual terminal, next to the Linux desktop you already use, with native GPU, input and audio.
- [Driving apps over the Bus](https://mixos.dev/drive.md): How an agent drives a native MixOS app through Bus verbs, from the widget tree and injected input to window commands and captures, with BusViewer as the worked example.
- [Decision — egui applications, engine first](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-09-egui-applications.md): MixOS applications and desktop furniture are built on egui and wgpu, with behaviour in engines and every action a named command reachable from the UI, the command line and the Bus.
- [Decision — source layout and naming](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-04-source-layout.md): Why the MixOS repository is laid out by kind of artefact (apps, services, cli, libs) with plain, unique names and self-contained components, and what was rejected.
- [Backdrop](https://mixos.dev/backdrop.md): The MixOS desktop background — drawn by its own program on the compositor's background layer, on every output, at native and fractional scale.
- [Bridging external applications](https://mixos.dev/bridge.md): How bridged puts an external application with a line-delimited JSON control channel on the Bus, one instance per application, and what that exposes.
- [Desktop settings have one native ABP authority](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-07-settings-authority.md): Status: accepted architecture, implementation staged. Contract version 0.1.0.
- [Decision — .mix programs and .mx documents](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-08-mix-programs-and-documents.md): Two Mix file families distinguish executable programs from declarative documents without multiplying script dialects.
- [Decision — the chrome family and chrome schemes](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-09-chrome-family-and-schemes.md): The design gains a typed chrome family of exact, non-derived colour roles, and three chrome schemes whose light and dark modes step the interface brightness.
- [Decision — icons and type](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-09-icons-and-type.md): MixOS applications use Lucide icons and the Inter and JetBrains Mono typefaces, with type weight and icon stroke as design tokens so a lighter profile is a design change.
- [Decision — Mix components](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-10-mix-components.md): A component may be written entirely in Mix. Its identity lives in a component.mx document instead of a Cargo package, and the component gates read both.
- [Decision — scheme and style are separate axes](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-10-scheme-and-style-axes.md): A theme is chosen on independent axes (scheme for the colours, style for the chrome's forms, mode, contrast), with window decorations and caption side beside them, so any palette can take any style.
- [Decision — style tokens as data](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-10-style-tokens-as-data.md): The forms and lengths of application chrome move out of renderer code into a typed style family in the design, so a new style is new data.
- [Decision — compd's module layout on entry](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-11-compd-module-layout.md): compd's crates enter with every mod.rs renamed to the 2018 layout; their self-named module files stay as a recorded, shrinking exception.
- [Decision — executed commands are published](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-11-executed-commands.md): Every MixOS application publishes each command it runs as a Bus topic, so what a person does by hand can be watched and recorded like what an agent does over the Bus.
- [Key bindings are desktop settings](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-11-keymaps-in-settings.md): Status: accepted. Settings contract 0.4.0 (additive). Widens Desktop settings have one native ABP authority, whose scope was the desktop's appearance and…
- [Decision — rec and play](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-11-rec-and-play.md): One command-line tool, recplay, installed as rec and play. play opens anything with the handler the desktop already knows, performs scripts and draws saved state. rec writes what happens on the desktop as an editable Mix script. rec and play are accepted name collisions.
- [The settings authority stays a separate service on noded](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-11-settings-authority-stays-a-service.md): Status: accepted. Builds on Desktop settings have one native ABP authority.
- [Settings snapshot schema 2 sends each design once](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-11-settings-snapshot-schema-2.md): Status: accepted. Settings contract 0.3.0 (additive), snapshot schema 2 beside schema 1. Follows plain followers read a summary.
- [Plain settings followers read a summary, not the snapshot](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-11-settings-summary-reads.md): Status: accepted. Settings contract 0.2.0 (additive). Builds on Desktop settings have one native ABP authority.
- [Decision — verb classes](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-11-verb-classes.md): Every registered Bus verb declares a class (intent, query, input or system), so tools that watch the Bus can tell a person's or agent's intent from reads, synthetic input and plumbing without guessing.
- [Decision — hostd, the host service](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-12-hostd.md): One root service per host answers host information and carries out privileged host actions through closed, typed, reversible verbs, so agents can act autonomously without sudo.
- [Decision — non-root install, per-service users, mesh-first ports](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-12-non-root-install-and-service-ports.md): MixOS installs and updates without root after a one-time bootstrap. Server daemons run as their own unprivileged users, listen on the WireGuard mesh by default, and get privileged ports from systemd rather than from file capabilities or root.
- [Decision — one repository, install profiles](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-12-one-repository-install-profiles.md): Server programs and the desktop stay in one MixOS repository and one Cargo workspace. The split between them is made where it matters, in what gets built and installed, by install profiles that every shipping component declares.
- [Decision — one system binary](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-12-one-system-binary.md): The mix shell and every headless MixOS daemon ship as one binary, built by cli/system and installed as mix. Each daemon is a symlink named after its component, and the binary picks what to run from the name it was started as. Components keep their own crates, tests, units and versions.
- [Decision — scene strings until Mix reads Fluent](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-12-scene-strings.md): Mix Scenes content (share/scenes) keeps its user-visible English strings in one table per scene library until Mix can read Fluent catalogues; then each table becomes that scene's en catalogue and its lookup reads the catalogue.
- [Decision — screenshot](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-12-screenshot.md): The screenshot and annotation app is named screenshot (app id dev.mixos.screenshot) and supersedes Cap, whose names are retired. Print Screen starts it. screenshot is an accepted binary-name collision with nwg-shell's helper.
- [Decision — shipped system dialogs](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-12-system-dialogs.md): Besides the Scene Editor, a shipped scene template that is hidden and declares a dialog may load as a dialog (a system dialog, such as the pager's rename prompt). It is enabled only while it shows, so the single dialog seat stays free.
- [Bundled fallback font licences](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-13-bundled-font-licences.md): Status: accepted, 2026-10-13.
- [Decision — desk and deskd](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-13-desk-and-deskd.md): The desktop's applications ship as one multi-call binary, desk, and its session services as another, deskd. Each app and service keeps its name as a link, so nothing that calls them changes, and one copy of egui, wgpu and the rest serves them all.
- [Instance verb families (schema 3)](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-13-instance-verb-families.md): Status: accepted, 2026-10-13.
- [Decision — session icon stroke and type](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-14-session-icon-stroke-and-type.md): The desktop session can choose its icon stroke and its interface and monospace font families and weight, applied to every MixOS app through the settings profile.
- [Decision — site URL layout](https://mixos.dev/decisions/2026-10-16-site-url-layout.md): Every component's documentation lives at the top of mixos.dev under its own name, in HTML and Markdown at fixed addresses. Everything that is not a component lives under one /docs/ section, so the only names a component can never take are docs and v.

- [Edit service](https://mixos.dev/edit.md): editd registers the edit service and serves the edit.v1 contract. Ced and agents share its buffers through native ABP. The service is headless and requires no…
- [email](https://mixos.dev/email.md): email (dev.mixos.email) is the reserved MixOS mail client: a pure JMAP client speaking HTTPS to any RFC 8620/8621-shaped server — the mesh's own maild, or…
- [The host service](https://mixos.dev/hostd.md): How hostd answers questions about the host and carries out privileged host changes through closed, typed verbs behind standing grants, receipts and rollback, so agents never need sudo.
